pages.title: Marine work, from workshop to onboard.
pages.intro: Seafort supports vessels and offshore structures with repair, maintenance, fabrication and installation. Our work connects workshop preparation with the tasks carried out on board.

sections.title: Services that work together
sections.body: Steel repairs, surface preparation, coatings and equipment installation often share the same work area. We bring these activities together with underwater services and technical supply.

sections.title: People and coordination
sections.body: The technical team, equipment and access arrangements are planned around the vessel and the work location. Coordination connects each activity with the next.

sections.title: Tell us what needs doing
sections.body: Send the asset details, location, drawings and planned dates. Our team can review the repair or installation support you need.

pages.title: Our Values
pages.intro: Clear communication, attention to the work and care for people guide our approach to marine and offshore projects.

sections.title: Communicate changes clearly

sections.title: Pay attention to the details

sections.title: Safety and environmental responsibility
sections.body: Site risks, access and environmental controls are considered when planning the work. The people involved need to understand the task and the procedures that apply.

pages.title: Maintenance & Repair
pages.intro: Steel renewal, tank and deck preparation, protective coatings and piping work for vessels and offshore assets.

sections.title: Steel and structural repairs
sections.body: Corroded or damaged steel is cut out and replaced to the engineering drawings. Workshop preparation is followed by onboard welding, grinding and finishing to suit the existing structure.

sections.title: Surface preparation and coatings
sections.body: Work can include debris removal, high-pressure water washing, drying and blasting to the specified Sa 2½ preparation grade. Spray coating is complemented by brush, roller and local touch-up application.
list: Tank and deck washing and cleaning
Spray, brush, roller and touch-up coatings

sections.title: Piping, equipment and installation
sections.body: Pipe supports are prepared, welded and installed for the work location. Piping connections and equipment supports are coordinated with the surrounding installation.
list: Piping and valve repair or replacement

sections.title: Access and inspection
sections.body: Scaffolding is erected and modified as the steelwork and surface treatment progress. Access, inspection and handover requirements are established with the project team.

pages.cover_alt: Workers carrying out steelwork on a fabricated structural assembly
pages.detail_title: From steel renewal to final coating.

sections.title: Inspection and survey support

sections.title: Hull, propeller and appendage work
sections.body: The method depends on inspection findings, coating compatibility and the conditions at the work location.
list: Propeller inspection, polishing and repair support

sections.title: Operational planning
sections.body: Diving, lifting and vessel operations need to be coordinated. Weather, access and operating restrictions are reviewed before the work is arranged.

sections.title: Request underwater support

overview.title: Responsibility begins with the way we work.
overview.body: Marine repair brings people, materials and equipment together in demanding environments. Our approach focuses on practical choices within each project: understanding the repair, preparing the team and considering the surrounding work area.

pillars.title: From the asset to the work site.
pillars.intro: These priorities connect workshop preparation with the work carried out on board.

items.title: Repair with purpose
items.body: Consider repair and component renewal against the engineering scope, helping owners maintain existing marine assets.
items.image_alt: Worker grinding a steel component from scaffold access

items.title: Prepare people for the task
items.body: Bring the required trades, access arrangements and responsibilities into the work plan before activities begin.
items.image_alt: Welders working on steel components at a marine worksite

items.title: Make resources count
items.body: Plan material needs and consider housekeeping, containment and work residues alongside fabrication and coating activities.
items.image_alt: Prepared steel gratings arranged in a work area

approach.title: Build responsibility into the work sequence.
approach.body: A clear scope connects preparation, execution and handover. Drawings, site conditions and the interfaces between trades help shape the plan. Environmental and safety arrangements are discussed with the vessel or shipyard organisation as part of that process.
approach.image_alt: Personnel coordinating assembly work on board a vessel

commitments.title: Small decisions shape the whole job.
commitments.intro: Practical priorities to carry through each agreed work scope.

items.title: Prepare before mobilising
items.body: Clarify drawings, access and work interfaces so the team understands the task and its sequence.

items.title: Plan for materials and residues
items.body: Consider cutting, preparation, reusable items and waste handover within the site arrangements.

items.title: Keep information clear
items.body: Agree the records and handover information needed for the work. Describe outcomes using project evidence.
